chunk_findings.detail: `_only_ids` returns `True` for any title where every `\w+` token merely contains at least one digit — it never compares the title to the item’s actual id or an id grammar. For example, an item with title `"l10n"` (a real localization title) or `"iPhone15"` has no non-digit word, so `_only_ids` returns `True`. `_untitled` then reports that item as having “no title of their own, only the id,” which is false and turns the doctor note into a false positive for meaningful alphanumeric titles.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health_notes.py:_only_ids

chunk_findings.detail: The test no longer exercises the MCP `ddflow_complete` path it is named after and that the bug report lists. It now calls `run_cli(repo, "complete", "T1", "--force", "--model", "x")` and asserts CLI stdout rather than calling `_call(repo, "ddflow_complete", ...)` and checking `body["progress"]`. A future change that makes MCP `ddflow_complete` return `{"ok": True}` without a `progress` field on successful forced completion will still leave this test green, so the MCP regression is no longer covered.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_progress_line_mcp.py:31-32 (test_mcp_complete_carries_the_progress_block)

chunk_findings.detail: `test_mcp_complete_carries_the_progress_block` no longer calls MCP. It runs CLI `complete T1 --force --model x` and only checks that stdout contains `Progress: tasks 1/1 (100%)`. An MCP `ddflow_complete` result that omits the `progress` key (the contract the old assertion `body["progress"].startswith("Progress: tasks 1/1 (100%)")` enforced) still passes. Sharing `finish.complete` does not cover MCP serialization of that block, so the named regression is gone.

chunk_findings.detail: The predicate is meant to match titles that are only an id, but `all(any(c.isdigit() for c in word) for word in re.findall(r"\w+", title))` returns `True` for any single word that merely contains a digit, even when the word is a real title. For example `_only_ids("OAuth2")` yields `True`, so `_untitled` will emit “no title of their own, only the id” and suggest `ddflow update <id> --title ...` for an item already titled `"OAuth2"`. It needs to distinguish id-shaped tokens such as `B30` from digit-containing words for the doctor note to be correct.
chunk_findings.title: ddflow/api/reporting/health_notes.py:_only_ids

chunk_findings.detail: The test no longer calls the MCP endpoint `ddflow_complete` at all: it invokes the CLI `complete` command and asserts on CLI stdout. If the MCP response for `ddflow_complete` stops carrying the `"progress"` key, this test still passes because it never inspects an MCP reply. The comment's claim that `_OPTIONAL_KEYS` covers this is not sufficient: `_OPTIONAL_KEYS` says a key can be merged when present, not that `ddflow_complete` actually produces `"progress"`. A regression where `ddflow_complete` returns `{"ok": True}` with no `"progress"` field is no longer caught, leaving the named MCP contract untested.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_progress_line_mcp.py:test_mcp_complete_carries_the_progress_block

chunk_findings.detail: `test_mcp_complete_carries_the_progress_block` no longer calls MCP. The old assertion was `body = _call(repo, "ddflow_complete", {"id": "T1", "force": True})` then `body["progress"]`. The replacement only runs `run_cli(..., "complete", "T1", "--force", ...)` and searches CLI stdout. Given an MCP `ddflow_complete` reply that omits `progress` (the failure this test is named for), the new test still passes, so the red case is no longer gated.
chunk_findings.title: tests/test_progress_line_mcp.py:34
